1.pericope_label: Get a potter’s earthen bottle, and go forth into the valley
debates: Which gate is meant by the name in the second verse
How this sign differs from the earlier one at the potter’s house
Whether a verb has dropped out before the mention of the elders
outliers: Calvin inclines to the solar sense of the gate’s name while conceding that the valley lay south of the city, not east
themes: A vessel past reshaping and fit only to be broken
Rulers summoned to witness their own ruin
Repetition designed to leave the obstinate inexcusable
A place of past idolatry chosen for the sign

3.pericope_label: Hear the word of the LORD, O kings of Judah
debates: Which king is reigning when the sign is given
Whether the innocent blood means the child sacrifices or judicial murders
Why kings are addressed in the plural
outliers: Gill takes the reigning king to be Zedekiah, where Ellicott and Clarke both name Jehoiakim
themes: A prophet commanded to show no respect of persons
Additions to worship counted as forsaking it
A place consecrated and then alienated
An earlier sanctuary’s ruin held up as the pattern

6.pericope_label: This place shall be called the valley of slaughter
debates: What the name of the valley derives from
Whether the counsel made void is political or religious
Whether the bottle was emptied as well as broken
outliers: Ellicott reports a view that the prophet poured water from the jar at this point, an act the text does not record
themes: A place of confidence renamed a place of slaughter
A verb chosen to echo the object in the prophet’s hand
Invention condemned by the absence of any command
Superstition credited with the appearance of wisdom

8.pericope_label: I will make this city desolate, and an hissing
debates: Whether the word means desolation or astonishment
Which siege the famine described belongs to
Whether the hissing marks scorn or detestation
outliers: Clarke refers the prediction forward to the Roman siege, where the others keep it to the Babylonian
themes: A threat enlarged because a single sentence would not be felt
Judgment attributed to God rather than to circumstance
Curses of the law reappearing as prophecy
Punishment shaped to answer the sin exactly

10.pericope_label: Even so will I break this people and this city
debates: Whether the breaking is final for the nation or only for that generation
Which destruction of the city the sign points to
Why a sign is added to a message already delivered
outliers: Ellicott holds that divine compassion exceeded what the parable could represent, where Calvin insists the ruin was wholly irremediable
themes: A hardened vessel worse off than soft clay
Sight used where hearing had failed
Signs held useless without doctrine attached
Confidence in a building that had itself been profaned

12.pericope_label: I will even make this city as Tophet
debates: What the name of the valley conveys when applied to the city
Whether the preposition in the last clause is causal or explanatory
Why roofs were used for worship of the host of heaven
outliers: Calvin holds that the message wounded the consciences of hearers who rejected it, so that they were miserable before the event
themes: The city made to resemble the place it had polluted
Splendour named in order to be dismissed
Defilement by the bodies of the dead
Places of devotion turned to idolatry

14.pericope_label: Then came Jeremiah from Tophet and stood in the court
debates: Why the same message is delivered twice in two places
Whether the closing verse is the whole address or a summary of one
What the hardened neck is a figure for
outliers: Ellicott takes the final verse for the summary of a longer discourse the prophet did not think it necessary to report
themes: A message repeated because the hearers were slow
A sign given to a few, a sermon to all
Guilt extended from the city to the whole land
Clearer light leaving less excuse
